12: /// ## What it does
13: /// Checks for commented-out Python code.
14: ///
15: /// ## Why is this bad?
16: /// Commented-out code is dead code, and is often included inadvertently.
17: /// It should be removed.
18: ///
19: /// ## Known problems
20: /// Prone to false positives when checking comments that resemble Python code,
21: /// but are not actually Python code ([#4845]).
22: ///
23: /// ## Example
24: /// ```python
25: /// # print("Hello, world!")
26: /// ```
27: ///

48: /// ERA001
49: pub(crate) fn commented_out_code(
50:     diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
51:     locator: &Locator,
52:     comment_ranges: &CommentRanges,
53:     settings: &LinterSettings,
54: ) {
55:     let mut comments = comment_ranges.into_iter().peekable();
56:     // Iterate over all comments in the document.
57:     while let Some(range) = comments.next() {
58:         let line = locator.line_str(range.start());
59: 
60:         if is_script_tag_start(line) {
61:             if skip_script_comments(range, &mut comments, locator) {
62:                 continue;
63:             }
64:         }
65: 
66:         // Verify that the comment is on its own line, and that it contains code.
67:         if is_own_line_comment(line) && comment_contains_code(line, &settings.task_tags[..]) {
68:             let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(CommentedOutCode, range);
69:             diagnostic.set_fix(Fix::display_only_edit(Edit::range_deletion(
70:                 locator.full_lines_range(range),
71:             )));
72:             diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
73:         }
74:     }
75: }

77: /// Parses the rest of a [PEP 723](https://peps.python.org/pep-0723/)
78: /// script comment and moves `comments` past the script comment's end unless
79: /// the script comment is invalid.
80: ///
81: /// Returns `true` if it is a valid script comment.
82: fn skip_script_comments<I>(
83:     script_start: TextRange,
84:     comments: &mut std::iter::Peekable<I>,
85:     locator: &Locator,
86: ) -> bool
87: where
88:     I: Iterator<Item = TextRange>,
89: {
90:     let contents = locator.contents();
91:     let start_line_end = locator.full_line_end(script_start.end());
92:     let rest = locator.after(start_line_end);
93:     if rest.is_empty() {
94:         return false;
95:     }
96: 
97:     let index = locator.to_index();
98:     let line_count = index.line_count();
99:     let mut current_line = index.line_index(start_line_end);
100: 
101:     let mut end_offset: Option<TextSize> = None;
102:     while current_line.to_zero_indexed() < line_count {
103:         let range_start = index.line_start(current_line, contents);
104:         let range_end = index.line_end(current_line, contents);
105:         let line_range = TextRange::new(range_start, range_end);
106:         let full_line = locator.slice(line_range);
107:         let line = full_line.trim_end_matches(['\r', '\n']);
108:         let stripped = line.strip_prefix('#');
109: 
110:         let Some(without_hash) = stripped else {
111:             break;
112:         };
113:         let content = if without_hash.is_empty() {
114:             ""
115:         } else if let Some(without_space) = without_hash.strip_prefix(' ') {
116:             without_space
117:         } else {
118:             break;
119:         };
120: 
121:         if content == "///" {
122:             // > Precedence for an ending line # /// is given when the next line is not a valid
123:             // > embedded content line as described above.
124:             // > For example, the following is a single fully valid block:
125:             // > ```python
126:             // > # /// some-toml
127:             // > # embedded-csharp = """
128:             // > # /// <summary>
129:             // > # /// text
130:             // > # ///
131:             // > # /// </summary>
132:             // > # public class MyClass { }
133:             // > # """
134:             // > # ///
135:             // ````
136:             let next_line = current_line.saturating_add(1);
137:             if next_line.to_zero_indexed() < line_count {
138:                 let next_start = index.line_start(next_line, contents);
139:                 let next_end = index.line_end(next_line, contents);
140:                 let next_range = TextRange::new(next_start, next_end);
141:                 let next_full_line = locator.slice(next_range);
142:                 let next_text = next_full_line.trim_end_matches(['\r', '\n']);
143:                 let next_prefix = next_text.strip_prefix('#');
144:                 let next_is_valid_script_line = match next_prefix {
145:                     Some(rest) => rest.is_empty() || rest.starts_with(' '),
146:                     None => false,
147:                 };
148:                 if next_is_valid_script_line {
149:                     current_line = next_line.saturating_add(1);
150:                     continue;
151:                 }
152:             }
153:             end_offset = Some(range_end);
154:             break;
155:         }
156: 
157:         current_line = current_line.saturating_add(1);
158:     }
159: 
160:     // > Unclosed blocks MUST be ignored.
161:     let Some(end_offset) = end_offset else {
162:         return false;
163:     };
164: 
165:     // Skip over all script-comments.
166:     while let Some(comment) = comments.peek() {
167:         if comment.start() >= end_offset {
168:             break;
169:         }
170:         comments.next();
171:     }
172: 
173:     true
174: }

7: /// PEP 723 metadata as parsed from a `script` comment block.
8: ///
9: /// See: <https://peps.python.org/pep-0723/>
10: ///
11: /// Vendored from: <https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/debe67ffdb0cd7835734100e909b2d8f79613743/crates/uv-scripts/src/lib.rs#L283>
12: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Eq, PartialEq)]
13: pub struct ScriptTag {
14:     /// The content of the script before the metadata block.
15:     prelude: String,
16:     /// The metadata block.
17:     metadata: String,
18:     /// The content of the script after the metadata block.
19:     postlude: String,
20: }
21: 
22: impl ScriptTag {
23:     /// Given the contents of a Python file, extract the `script` metadata block with leading
24:     /// comment hashes removed, any preceding shebang or content (prelude), and the remaining Python
25:     /// script.
26:     ///
27:     /// Given the following input string representing the contents of a Python script:
28:     ///
29:     /// ```python
30:     /// #!/usr/bin/env python3
31:     /// # /// script
32:     /// # requires-python = '>=3.11'
33:     /// # dependencies = [
34:     /// #   'requests<3',
35:     /// #   'rich',
36:     /// # ]
37:     /// # ///
38:     ///
39:     /// import requests
40:     ///
41:     /// print("Hello, World!")
42:     /// ```
43:     ///
44:     /// This function would return:
45:     ///
46:     /// - Preamble: `#!/usr/bin/env python3\n`
47:     /// - Metadata: `requires-python = '>=3.11'\ndependencies = [\n  'requests<3',\n  'rich',\n]`
48:     /// - Postlude: `import requests\n\nprint("Hello, World!")\n`
49:     ///
50:     /// See: <https://peps.python.org/pep-0723/>
51:     pub fn parse(contents: &[u8]) -> Option<Self> {
52:         // Identify the opening pragma.
53:         let index = FINDER.find(contents)?;
54: 
55:         // The opening pragma must be the first line, or immediately preceded by a newline.
56:         if !(index == 0 || matches!(contents[index - 1], b'\r' | b'\n')) {
57:             return None;
58:         }
59: 
60:         // Extract the preceding content.
61:         let prelude = std::str::from_utf8(&contents[..index]).ok()?;
62: 
63:         // Decode as UTF-8.
64:         let contents = &contents[index..];
65:         let contents = std::str::from_utf8(contents).ok()?;
66: 
67:         let mut lines = contents.lines();
68: 
69:         // Ensure that the first line is exactly `# /// script`.
70:         if !lines.next().is_some_and(|line| line == "# /// script") {
71:             return None;
72:         }
73: 
74:         // > Every line between these two lines (# /// TYPE and # ///) MUST be a comment starting
75:         // > with #. If there are characters after the # then the first character MUST be a space. The
76:         // > embedded content is formed by taking away the first two characters of each line if the
77:         // > second character is a space, otherwise just the first character (which means the line
78:         // > consists of only a single #).
79:         let mut toml = vec![];
80: 
81:         // Extract the content that follows the metadata block.
82:         let mut python_script = vec![];
83: 
84:         while let Some(line) = lines.next() {
85:             // Remove the leading `#`.
86:             let Some(line) = line.strip_prefix('#') else {
87:                 python_script.push(line);
88:                 python_script.extend(lines);
89:                 break;
90:             };
91: 
92:             // If the line is empty, continue.
93:             if line.is_empty() {
94:                 toml.push("");
95:                 continue;
96:             }
97: 
98:             // Otherwise, the line _must_ start with ` `.
99:             let Some(line) = line.strip_prefix(' ') else {
100:                 python_script.push(line);
101:                 python_script.extend(lines);
102:                 break;
103:             };
104: 
105:             toml.push(line);
106:         }
107: 
108:         // Find the closing `# ///`. The precedence is such that we need to identify the _last_ such
109:         // line.
110:         //
111:         // For example, given:
112:         // ```python
113:         // # /// script
114:         // #
115:         // # ///
116:         // #
117:         // # ///
118:         // ```
119:         //
120:         // The latter `///` is the closing pragma
121:         let index = toml.iter().rev().position(|line| *line == "///")?;
122:         let index = toml.len() - index;
123: 
124:         // Discard any lines after the closing `# ///`.
125:         //
126:         // For example, given:
127:         // ```python
128:         // # /// script
129:         // #
130:         // # ///
131:         // #
132:         // #
133:         // ```
134:         //
135:         // We need to discard the last two lines.
136:         toml.truncate(index - 1);
137: 
138:         // Join the lines into a single string.
139:         let prelude = prelude.to_string();
140:         let metadata = toml.join("\n") + "\n";
141:         let postlude = python_script.join("\n") + "\n";
142: 
143:         Some(Self {
144:             prelude,
145:             metadata,
146:             postlude,
147:         })
148:     }
149: }

part.text:
The bug is in `skip_script_comments` (crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/eradicate/rules/commented_out_code.rs): it treats `# ///` as the block end only when the *next* line isn't a valid script comment line. When trailing comments like `#` / `# Bla bla bla` follow the closing `# ///`, the end is never recognized, the block looks unclosed, and the metadata lines get flagged. The canonical PEP 723 parser (`crates/ruff_python_ast/src/script.rs:108-121`) instead treats the *last* `# ///` line in the comment run as the closing pragma.

Let me check the existing snapshot fixtures before changing behavior:

part.text:
Fixed. The issue example now lints clean.

**Cause:** `skip_script_comments` in `crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/eradicate/rules/commented_out_code.rs` treated a `# ///` line as the block terminator only when the *next* line wasn't a valid script comment line. With trailing comments after the metadata block (`#`, `# Bla bla bla`, ...), the closing `# ///` was misread as content, the block appeared unclosed (PEP 723: unclosed blocks are ignored), and ERA001 flagged the metadata lines.

**Fix:** Follow the canonical PEP 723 parsing semantics used in `crates/ruff_python_ast/src/script.rs:108-121` — scan the contiguous comment run and treat the *last* `# ///` line as the closing pragma (commented_out_code.rs:121-135).

**Validation:** all 13 eradicate unit tests pass, including the fixture case "Script tag block followed by normal block (OK)" that reproduces this exact issue, and the real `ruff check --select ERA001` run on the issue's example reports "All checks passed".
